title: Scientists Revived Tardigrades After 30 Years Frozen in Antarctic Moss

scenes.text: A moss sample sat frozen for thirty years. Something inside woke up.
Japanese scientists collected it in Antarctica in 1983 and stored it at minus 20 degrees.
In 2014 they thawed it. Two tardigrades and an egg were inside.
One adult started crawling and eating within about two weeks. It laid 19 eggs, and 14 hatched.
The frozen egg hatched too, and that baby grew up and had babies of its own.
Frozen for thirty years. Then it had a family.

description:
Tardigrades from Antarctic moss frozen for more than 30 years were revived and went on to reproduce.
The moss was collected in 1983, kept at minus 20 degrees Celsius, thawed in 2014, and one adult laid 19 eggs, 14 of which hatched. An egg also hatched and reproduced.
Would you want to be frozen for 30 years? Comment below.
first_comment: Tardigrades have also survived the vacuum of space. What do you think is the toughest animal on Earth?
